seoTitle: Meta Refresh Redirect Detector with 301 Rule
metaDescription: Find meta refresh tags in pasted HTML, see delay and target, how Google reads them, and the server redirect rule to use. Free.
intro: Finds meta refresh tags and explains what they do for SEO.
why:
A meta refresh can redirect a visitor without a server rule. Google reads an instant refresh as a permanent redirect and a delayed one as temporary, but server-side redirects are more reliable.

The tool shows delay and target and writes an Apache and nginx rule for the page path you enter. A timed redirect can also hurt users: WCAG technique F40 lists it as a failure.
howTo: Enter the path of the page for the server rules.
Replace the refresh with the server redirect if you can.

faq.a: Google treats instant as permanent and delayed as temporary, per its documentation.
No. Only HTML tags can be seen here.
It is faster, clearer to crawlers and does not flash a page.

faq.q: What if there is no URL?
faq.a: The page reloads itself; the tool warns about that.
